title: Affine spectrum tensor coordinate homology transport
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to S'$, $g:S'\to S$, $g':X'\to X$ be a cartesian square of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], and suppose their spectrum maps on global sections also form a cartesian square. Fix sheaf derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], a complex $P$ of modules on $X$, $z_0\in\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X',\top)$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$. Put $j=X'.\mathrm{isoSpec}^{-1}$, $z=j(z_0)$, $P_0=(X.\mathrm{isoSpec}^{-1})^*P$ and $P_g=(g')^*P$ termwise. Write $R,A,B,D$ and $R_0,A_0,B_0,D_0$ for the two sets of four stalk rings and their structural maps [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition], $Q=P_{g'(z)}$, $Q_0=(P_0)_{g'_0(z_0)}$, and $V=D\otimes_A Q$, $V_0=D_0\otimes_{A_0}Q_0$ for tensorComplex. Suppose supplied ring isomorphisms $e_R,e_A,e_B,e_D$, commuting with the R-to-A and R-to-B maps and satisfying $e_D(\mu(a\otimes b))=\mu_0(e_A(a)\otimes e_B(b))$, and supplied chain isomorphisms $q:Q\cong\operatorname{Res}_{e_A}Q_0$, $t:V\cong\operatorname{Res}_{e_D}V_0$ with $t^k(d\otimes x)=e_D(d)\otimes q^k(x)$. Let $F,F_0$ forget scalars to additive groups, $c_i:H^i(\operatorname{Res}_{e_D}V_0)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{e_D}H^i(V_0)$ be exact restriction homology, $s,s_0$ the tensorStalkIso maps [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition], and $\alpha:(g'_0)^*P_0\cong j^*P_g$ the ordinary pullback composition isomorphism [def-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-iso]. Let $U$ be the additive ordinary homology isomorphism along $j$, constructed by conjugating homology of isoPullbackAdditiveStalkIso [lem-pc-iso-pullback-stalk-cohomology] by exact additive stalk cohomology factors and comparisonStalkHomologyIso. Then $F(H^i(t));F(c_i);F_0(H^i(s_0))=F(H^i(s));U;F_0(H^i((\operatorname{stalk}_{z_0}\alpha^{-1})))$. This is solely a statement about stalk rings and ordinary complexes; it asserts nothing about a derived tensor cohomology source or its counit. Require in addition Fc(t);rho;F0c(s0)=Fc(s);Uchain;F0c(stalk(alpha inverse)), where Uchain is the canonical pullback-stalk complex comparison and rho identifies forgotten restriction of scalars. Then the displayed homology equation holds for these supplied data.
